VTS Scoring Log

Umbrella Labs

US-based vendor · Operating since late 2010s· Scored August 2026· umbrellalabs.is

Umbrella Labs has operated since the late 2010s and was among the early vendors to publish third-party COAs at a time when most competitors did not. Today its catalog spans 127 peptides with COAs from NCCCCE-credentialed chemists publicly accessible on each product page. Credit card processing is active through the MESH network. The long operational track record and catalog depth are the primary differentiators; the absence of a named testing lab limits the traceability score.

81 /100
High Transparency
Third-party COAs from NCCCCE-credentialed chemists, 127-compound public catalog, operating since the late 2010s with an established community presence. Largest catalog on the current roster.

Community Signal
Independent Test Results
Multiple community-sourced test results exist from research forums over the years given the long operational history. Results have been generally positive for core compounds. No major systematic quality failure flagged in reviewed sources as of August 2026.
Community Experience
Community feedback is mixed across review sources. Positive signals include reliable fulfillment and catalog breadth. Negative signals include inconsistent customer service experiences noted in multiple independent reviews. Buyers should consult current forum discussion as part of their own evaluation.
Scoring Notes
NCCCCE-credentialed chemists - credential, not a named lab
COAs are described as produced by NCCCCE-credentialed chemists. This is a credential designation rather than a specific named laboratory. It confirms the chemist's professional qualification but does not provide a lab name or public verification portal that an outsider can use to cross-check a specific COA result.
127-compound catalog - testing coverage at breadth is harder to confirm
Broad catalog claims of full-catalog COA coverage are harder to sustain across 127 compounds than across a 30-compound catalog. The existence of a public archive with dated entries across a large SKU set is a positive signal, but some entries date to 2023, which may warrant direct confirmation for older compounds.
Credit card via MESH - $1,000 per order cap
Credit card processing is active through the MESH network. Charges appear as 'UNBLOCK' on bank statements. The per-order cap and third-party payment routing are noted for buyer awareness, but credit card acceptance remains a legitimacy signal relative to crypto-only vendors.
Mixed community reviews captured in signal, not score
Community feedback is mixed. This is captured in the Community Signal section above, not in the process-transparency score. VTS dimensions score only verifiable process inputs, not community sentiment.
